chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from some of his companions, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Ali ibn Uqbah, from Musa ibn Uqayl, from some of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

In a sheep that drank urine, then was slaughtered, he said: What is in its stomach should be washed out, then there is no harm with it. And likewise, if it ate excrement, as long as it is not a 'Jallalah', and the Jallalah is that which that [excrement/urine] is its food.

key_terms.جَلَّالَة: An animal that feeds primarily on excrement or urine, affecting the taste and purity of its meat
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it (permissible)
key_terms.يُغْسَلُ: It is washed (referring to washing out the stomach contents)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of a sheep permissible if it drank urine, and what is the definition of a Jallalah animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the definition of 'Jallalah' by distinguishing between incidental consumption of excrement and it being the primary diet, thereby permitting the meat if the stomach is washed. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that impurity (najāsah) does not automatically render meat haram unless the animal's sustenance is predominantly impure, a nuance critical in fiqh al-Jallalah. It underscores the practical application of purification (taharah) in food preparation within Shia legal tradition.
